evidence: 2025 da Vinci procedures increased 18% to ~3.153 million; Q2 2026 procedures increased 15% y/y to ~889,000.
OUS da Vinci procedures grew 20% y/y in Q2 2026, with strength in India, Italy and the UK; adoption remains materially earlier-stage than the U.S.
da Vinci 5 had an installed base of 1,710 systems at 2026-06-30, only 136 outside the U.S., leaving a multi-year global replacement/adoption runway.
Ion Q2 2026 biopsy procedures increased ~36% y/y to ~47,900, providing a second robotic platform beyond soft-tissue surgery.
counter_evidence: U.S. da Vinci procedure growth slowed to ~12% in Q2 2026 from ~14% in Q2 2025.
China placements are being pressured by domestic competitors, industrial policy and tender/governance constraints.
missing_data: Independent global robotic-surgery market share by procedure and geography

evidence: Procedure adoption continues across general surgery, gynecology and urology, while the company cites growing clinical and economic evidence and surgeon training as adoption drivers.
da Vinci instruments and accessories generate recurring per-procedure economics, while service contracts and system leasing lower customer adoption friction.
Japan added reimbursement for seven da Vinci procedures in 2026, including inguinal hernia repair, and added incremental reimbursement for high-volume robotic programs.
counter_evidence: Hospital capital budgets, staffing, reimbursement and total procedure economics can constrain adoption.
More than half of da Vinci procedures are for benign conditions, increasing cost sensitivity and seasonality.
missing_data: Independent procedure-level cost-effectiveness comparisons across major indications

evidence: Recurring revenue was 85% of revenue in Q2 and H1 2026, linking economics to installed base, utilization, consumables, service and leases.
At 2025 year-end the da Vinci installed base was ~11,106 systems; the ecosystem includes systems, instruments, stapling, energy, vision, training, field service and digital tools.
Clinical-sales and service organizations are embedded at hospital accounts, increasing workflow integration and switching friction.
da Vinci 5, SP and Ion expand the platform while preserving common ecosystem economics.
counter_evidence: Medtronic, Johnson & Johnson, CMR Surgical and multiple Chinese robotic-surgery companies are active or prospective competitors.
China already shows a local example of moat pressure through domestic competition and industrial policy.
Usage-based leases can make upgrades easier but may also lower switching friction if competing systems become credible.
missing_data: Third-party surgeon retention and multi-vendor hospital adoption data

evidence: 2025 operating cash flow was $3.03B and simple FCF proxy (CFO less PP&E purchases) was ~$2.49B.
H1 2026 operating cash flow increased to $1.97B from $1.30B; simple H1 FCF proxy was ~$1.76B.
Shares outstanding declined from 355.1M at 2025 year-end to 353.9M at 2026-06-30 despite share-based compensation.
High recurring consumables/service mix and gross margins support strong incremental cash economics.
counter_evidence: Leasing shifts system economics from upfront cash to multi-year recovery and requires balance-sheet capital.
Inventory and operating-lease asset build mean CFO-minus-capex is an imperfect measure of economic free cash flow.
H1 2026 share-based compensation expense was $426M pre-tax, a material cost of retaining talent.
missing_data: Company-reported incremental ROIC by growth investment cohort

evidence: Dave Rosa became CEO in 2025 after a multi-year succession process; Gary Guthart moved to Executive Chair and Craig Barratt serves as Lead Independent Director.
Executive PSUs are explicitly linked to multi-year procedure growth and relative adjusted operating margin.
The company maintains a debt-light balance sheet while funding R&D, manufacturing capacity, vertical integration and acquisitions from operating cash flow.
H1 2026 repurchases of $1.44B more than offset equity issuance/dilution at the share-count level.
counter_evidence: 2025 repurchases averaged $477.84 per share, materially above the September 2026 reference price near $370, raising questions about repurchase timing.
Share-based compensation remains substantial.
July 2026 bylaw amendments increased procedural requirements around shareholder nominations and proposals, a modest governance watch item.
missing_data: Post-transition capital allocation track record under CEO Dave Rosa over a full cycle

evidence: At 2026-06-30 cash plus short- and long-term investments were ~$8.63B versus total liabilities of ~$2.58B.
The balance sheet reports no conventional funded debt line and operations are strongly cash generative.
The company states it expects to fund future growth from cash generated by operations.
counter_evidence: Leasing expansion, acquisitions, manufacturing investment and supplier commitments consume capital and increase asset intensity.
Tariffs, supply-chain disruptions or hospital spending shocks can compress margins and cash flow.

evidence: At the 2026-09-03 close of $369.83, market capitalization is approximately $130.7B using 353.278M shares outstanding.
The share price is materially below the January 2026 52-week high, reducing but not eliminating valuation risk.
A base reverse-DCF/DCF framework using LTM simple FCF of ~$3.22B produces a base fair value near $398 per share.
counter_evidence: Current enterprise value is roughly 38x LTM simple FCF and market capitalization roughly 42x LTM attributable net income.
Reverse DCF indicates the market still requires roughly 11%-13% annual FCF growth for a decade depending on terminal multiple assumptions of 20x-25x at a 10% discount rate.
Base-case upside is only high-single digits, leaving limited margin of safety despite excellent business quality.
missing_data: Market-consensus long-term estimates intentionally excluded from primary underwriting

evidence: Robotic-assisted surgery remains a global penetration story, and da Vinci 5/SP/Ion create multiple growth vectors on top of a large installed base.
Net cash, high recurring revenue and strong cash generation reduce bankruptcy/permanent-capital-loss risk.
counter_evidence: At an approximately $131B market capitalization, a 10x outcome requires a very large future earnings base and is less plausible than it was earlier in the company lifecycle.
Scenario analysis at the reference price shows meaningful downside in a de-rating case versus only modest base-case upside.
missing_data: Long-run TAM and penetration by procedure with independent validation
